market.title: EU Instant Payments Regulation: CEE Banks Accelerate Compliance
market.summary_short: The EU Instant Payments Regulation is driving rapid changes in CEE banking, with banks prioritizing compliance ahead of upcoming deadlines. This includes significant infrastructure upgrades and operational adjustments to meet the new requirements.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's Instant Payments Regulation, which mandates the availability of instant credit transfers in Euro within 10 seconds, is causing a significant push for compliance across CEE banks. While the initial deadline for receiving instant payments was early 2025, the full scope, including sending capabilities and fee parity with standard transfers, is approaching. Banks in the CEE region, including those in the RBI network, are investing heavily in upgrading their payment infrastructure, ensuring 24/7/365 processing capabilities, and integrating with national instant payment schemes. Challenges include liquidity management for continuous processing and ensuring seamless integration with corporate treasury systems. The regulation aims to boost the adoption of instant payments across Europe, enhancing speed and efficiency for both consumers and businesses.
key_points: EU Instant Payments Regulation mandates 10-second Euro credit transfers.
CEE banks are heavily investing in infrastructure upgrades for 24/7/365 processing.
Upcoming deadlines require banks to offer instant payment sending and receiving at standard transfer fees.
Liquidity management and corporate system integration are key implementation challenges.
market.rbi_cash_management: This regulation is critical for RBI Cash Management as CMIplus must fully support instant payments across all CEE network banks. It necessitates continuous platform enhancements, API integrations, and ensuring seamless liquidity management for corporate clients utilizing instant payment rails.

market.title: PSD3 Proposal: Enhanced Open Banking and Fraud Prevention
market.summary_short: The latest PSD3 proposal from the European Commission aims to strengthen Open Banking frameworks and introduce more robust fraud prevention measures. This includes stricter rules for payment service providers and improved data sharing mechanisms.
market.summary_detail: The European Commission's recent proposal for PSD3 (Payment Services Directive 3) and the Payment Services Regulation (PSR) signals a significant evolution for the European payments landscape. Key elements include further empowering Open Banking by refining access to account data and enhancing customer control over their financial information. Crucially for corporates, PSD3 introduces more stringent requirements for fraud prevention, such as mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP) services across all EU member states to combat authorized push payment (APP) fraud. The proposal also seeks to improve the regulatory consistency across the EU, ensuring a level playing field for all payment service providers and fostering innovation while maintaining high security standards. The legislative process is ongoing, with implementation expected in the coming years.
key_points: PSD3 proposal strengthens Open Banking and introduces new fraud prevention measures.
Mandatory Verification of Payee (VoP) services are proposed to combat APP fraud.
The directive aims to enhance customer control over financial data and improve regulatory consistency.
Implementation of PSD3 is anticipated to roll out over the next few years.
market.rbi_cash_management: PSD3 is a cornerstone for future CMIplus development, particularly regarding Open Banking APIs and fraud prevention features like VoP. RBI Cash Management must proactively adapt its platform to meet new compliance requirements and leverage enhanced data access for innovative client solutions.

market.title: AI-Powered Fraud Detection Transforms Corporate Payments Security
market.summary_short: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming indispensable in combating sophisticated payment fraud, offering advanced detection capabilities for corporate treasuries. New solutions leverage machine learning to identify anomalies and prevent financial losses in real-time.
market.summary_detail: The increasing sophistication of cybercrime and payment fraud schemes is pushing corporate treasuries to adopt advanced AI-powered solutions. These systems utilize machine learning algorithms to analyze vast amounts of payment data, identifying unusual patterns, behavioral anomalies, and potential fraud indicators that human analysts or rule-based systems might miss. Real-time monitoring and predictive analytics are key features, allowing for immediate flagging and blocking of suspicious transactions, particularly relevant for instant payments. Integration with existing Treasury Management Systems (TMS) and Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) platforms is crucial for seamless operation. While AI offers significant advantages in reducing financial losses and improving operational efficiency, challenges remain in data quality, model training, and avoiding false positives, requiring continuous refinement and expert oversight.
key_points: AI-powered systems use machine learning to detect sophisticated payment fraud.
Real-time monitoring and predictive analytics are crucial for instant payment security.
Integration with TMS/ERP systems is essential for effective fraud prevention.
Challenges include data quality, model training, and minimizing false positives.

This enhances security for corporate clients, reduces operational risk, and strengthens RBI's position as a trusted cash management partner, especially for high-volume, real-time transactions.

market.title: EU Mandates Instant Payments: Impact on Corporate Treasuries
market.summary_short: The EU's Instant Payments Regulation has been formally adopted, making instant payments mandatory across the SEPA zone. This move aims to accelerate payment processing and enhance liquidity for businesses.
market.summary_detail: The European Union's Instant Payments Regulation, recently published in the Official Journal, mandates that all payment service providers (PSPs) in the SEPA zone offer instant credit transfers. This regulation requires PSPs to ensure funds are credited to the recipient's account within ten seconds, regardless of the time or day. It also includes provisions for affordable pricing, ensuring instant payments are not more expensive than traditional credit transfers. The regulation's phased implementation will significantly impact corporate treasuries, requiring updates to payment systems, liquidity management strategies, and fraud prevention measures. The full transition to ISO 20022 for instant payments is a key enabler.

Mandatory 10-second processing for SEPA credit transfers.
Pricing must be comparable to standard credit transfers.
Phased implementation timeline for PSPs.

market.title: Getting the Most Out of ISO 20022
market.summary_short: Global adoption of ISO 20022 is progressing, but a significant standards update in November 2026 will require banks and corporates to adopt a more data-centric approach. This update will remove unstructured postal addresses, necessitating changes in payment messaging.
market.summary_detail: The XML-based ISO 20022 messaging standard has seen global adoption, spurred by Swift’s migration deadline last year and the launch of the US Fedwire Funds Service. This update mandates the removal of unstructured postal addresses from payment messages, pushing banks and corporate treasurers towards a more structured and data-centric approach. This change will impact how payment data is captured, processed, and transmitted, requiring system adjustments and potentially new data management strategies to ensure compliance and leverage the full benefits of the richer data standard.

regulatory.title: ECB Emphasizes Instant Payments within SEPA Framework
regulatory.summary_short: The ECB continues to promote instant payments as a key component of its retail payments strategy within the SEPA framework. This involves ongoing efforts to enhance the speed, efficiency, and reach of instant payment solutions across Europe.
regulatory.summary_detail: Under its retail payments strategy, the ECB highlights instant payments as a crucial area of focus within SEPA. This commitment aims to ensure that instant payment solutions become the norm, offering immediate fund transfers 24/7/365. Banks and payment service providers are expected to continuously adapt their infrastructure and services to support and promote instant payment adoption, aligning with the broader goal of a harmonized and efficient European payment landscape. This includes ensuring full compliance with SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) requirements.
key_points: Continuous push for wider adoption of SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst).
Focus on enhancing the reach and accessibility of instant payment services.
Ongoing development and refinement of the retail payments strategy.
Banks must ensure 24/7/365 availability for instant payment processing.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: CMIplus must ensure full compliance with SCT Inst requirements, optimize its instant payment processing capabilities, and explore value-added services built on instant payment rails for corporate clients in CEE. This includes leveraging ISO 20022 standards for enhanced data.

regulatory.title: ECB Continues Modernization of TARGET Services and Oversight
regulatory.summary_short: The ECB is actively working on the modernization of its TARGET Services (T2, T2S, TIPS) to ensure robust and efficient financial market infrastructure. This includes ongoing oversight of payment systems and critical service providers.
regulatory.summary_detail: The ECB maintains a strong focus on its TARGET Services, which include T2 for real-time gross settlement, T2S for securities settlement, and TIPS for instant payment settlement. The 'Payments news & events' section explicitly mentions news on 'TARGET Services' and 'work being done on new technologies in the area of wholesale central bank money settlement.' This indicates ongoing development and modernization efforts. Furthermore, the ECB's oversight function extends to payment systems, securities settlement systems, central counterparties, and critical service providers, ensuring their resilience and stability, including cyber resilience initiatives like TIBER-EU.
key_points: Ongoing modernization and enhancement of T2, T2S, and TIPS platforms.
Continuous oversight of critical payment systems and infrastructures.
Emphasis on cyber resilience through initiatives like TIBER-EU.
Banks must adapt to any new technical specifications or operational guidelines for TARGET Services.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management must stay informed about TARGET Services updates, particularly for T2 and TIPS, to ensure seamless connectivity, operational efficiency, and compliance with any new technical or oversight requirements for wholesale payments and liquidity management.

regulatory.title: EU Regulations IPR, PSD3, PSR Impact Liquidity Management
regulatory.summary_short: A new EBA report details how the Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), proposed PSD3, and Payment Services Regulation (PSR) will significantly transform liquidity management. These regulations are expected to accelerate instant payment adoption and foster a level playing field among financial institutions.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) has published a report by its Liquidity Management Working Group (LMWG) examining the profound implications of three key EU regulatory initiatives on liquidity management. The Instant Payments Regulation (IPR), the proposed Payment Services Regulation (PSR), and the proposed Payment Services Directive 3 (PSD3) are analysed for their expected impact. The report highlights how these measures will drive the uptake of instant payments, ensure competitive fairness among market participants, and fundamentally reshape the liquidity management landscape for banks. Financial institutions need to assess their current liquidity frameworks and prepare for operational adjustments to comply with the evolving regulatory environment.
key_points: Analyze impact of IPR, PSD3, PSR on liquidity management frameworks.
Prepare for accelerated instant payment adoption and related liquidity shifts.
Ensure compliance with new requirements for a level playing field.
Review operational adjustments needed for transformed liquidity landscape.
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management (CMIplus) must assess its liquidity management processes and systems in light of IPR, PSD3, and PSR. This includes evaluating real-time liquidity needs for instant payments and ensuring robust multi-currency liquidity management capabilities across CEE network banks.

regulatory.title: EBA Fraud Taxonomy Version 7.0 Effective January 2027
regulatory.summary_short: The EBA has released version 7.0 of its Fraud Taxonomy, effective 1 January 2027, to harmonise fraud scenario descriptions across Europe. This update reflects the latest fraud trends and will support pan-European fraud-fighting efforts, including data sharing under the forthcoming Payment Services Regulation.
regulatory.summary_detail: The Euro Banking Association (EBA) announced the publication of version 7.0 of its EBA Fraud Taxonomy, which will come into effect on 1 January 2027. Developed by the Expert Group on Payment Fraud-related Topics (EGPF), the taxonomy is updated annually to align with evolving fraud trends. Key updates in version 7.0 include replacing 'emotional manipulation' with more specific modi like 'support a friend or family member fraud', 'romance fraud', and 'charity / donation fraud', and adding new labels for suspected money mule activity and 'card chip relay' fraud. This harmonised framework is crucial for improving fraud monitoring, reporting, and information sharing, particularly in preparation for data sharing arrangements under the upcoming Payment Services Regulation (PSR), which is part of the PSD3 package.
key_points: Implement EBA Fraud Taxonomy v7.0 by 1 January 2027.
Update fraud monitoring and reporting systems to reflect new categories.
Prepare for enhanced data sharing requirements under forthcoming PSR/PSD3.
Train fraud experts on new fraud modi and labels (e.g., romance fraud, money mule activity).
regulatory.rbi_cash_management: RBI Cash Management (CMIplus) must integrate EBA Fraud Taxonomy v7.0 into its fraud detection and reporting systems by January 2027. This requires updating internal categorisation, ensuring compliance with future data sharing requirements under PSD3/PSR, and potentially adapting API specifications for fraud reporting.
